questions.question: What is the difference between var, let, and const?
questions.title: var, let, and const
questions.direct_answer: var is function-scoped and can be redeclared; let and const are block-scoped. let can be reassigned, while const cannot be reassigned after initialization, although an object or array referenced by const can still be mutated.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you understand modern JavaScript scope and reassignment.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling const objects immutable or using var in block-sensitive code.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention temporal dead zone behavior for let and const before initialization.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define var, let, and const simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Prefer block scope
sections.content: Modern JavaScript usually prefers `const` by default and `let` when reassignment is required. Both are block-scoped; `var` is function-scoped.

sections.title: Scope examples
Remember
items: Use const unless the binding changes.
Avoid var in new code because function scope and hoisting are easy to misuse.

sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content: `let` and `const` are block-scoped. `let` permits reassignment, while `const` protects the binding, not the referenced object's internals. `var` is function-scoped and redeclarable, so I avoid it in modern code.
